 Tesla News Elon Musk at Baron Conference Nov 6: What to Expect
 BASENOR Editorial Desk 
 Oct 28, 2026 
 Updated October 28, 2026 
 2 min read
 Share 
 Elon Musk is confirmed to appear at the Annual Baron Investment Conference on November 6, 2026, joining Baron Capital founder Ron Baron for a virtual fireside chat. The conversation is expected to cover Musk's vision for the future, his companies' trajectories, and the technologies he sees as most transformative. Here's what you need to know about the event.
 Source: @SawyerMerritt — October 28, 2026 
 When and where is this happening?
 The Annual Baron Investment Conference takes place on Friday, November 6, 2026, starting at 8:00 AM ET at the Metropolitan Opera House at Lincoln Center in New York City. Musk's fireside chat with Ron Baron is scheduled to begin at 1:10 PM ET (10:10 AM PT). The session with Musk will be conducted virtually — he won't be appearing on stage in person.
 Who is Ron Baron, and why does this pairing matter?
 Ron Baron is the Founder and CEO of Baron Capital, a growth-focused investment firm that has been one of Tesla's most prominent long-term institutional backers. Baron has held Tesla stock through years of volatility and has consistently made the case for Musk's long-term vision to his clients. A fireside chat between the two isn't a neutral interview — it's a conversation between an investor who has publicly staked his reputation on Musk's companies and the man running them. Expect candid, forward-looking discussion rather than a rehearsed press-conference tone.
 What topics are likely to come up?
 According to Baron Capital's official confirmation, the discussion will focus on future ideas and what's next for Musk's ventures. Based on the framing, that points toward Tesla's robotaxi and autonomous driving roadmap, Optimus robot production, xAI and Grok's development trajectory, and SpaceX's ongoing Starship program. Baron conferences have historically given Musk room to speak expansively — past appearances have produced some of his more detailed public comments on timelines and strategy.
 Can Tesla owners or retail investors watch it?
 Attendance at the Baron Investment Conference is restricted to Baron Capital's clients and shareholders. To qualify, shareholders must have held a minimum investment value of $40,000 in Baron Funds as of June 30, 2026, with new accounts eligible if established by October 30, 2026. Registration opened August 17, 2026. If you don't meet those criteria, the event is not publicly streamed — though notable quotes and clips from Musk's session typically circulate on X shortly after.
 Why should Tesla owners pay attention to this?
 Musk's appearances at investor-focused events often yield more specific forward guidance than standard earnings calls or social media posts. When he sits down with a long-term believer like Baron, the conversation tends to surface concrete timelines, product priorities, and candid assessments of where things stand. For anyone tracking Tesla's autonomous vehicle rollout, Optimus production scaling, or the broader direction of xAI, this is worth monitoring closely on November 6.
